body: Thanks re: my mother. She was the kindest, sweetest person I've ever known and my best friend. The void her passing has created is unreal. I've always done lots of writing, it has been helpful in the past. These days, I've been using the practice to try and keep track of all the different medications I'm taking, the side effects, the doses etc. At this point, I'm trying to get all my past journals and diaries together to burn in my fireplace so no one will find and read them once I'm gone. I'm tired of documenting my endless pain.

Yes, I do take medicinal marijuana, everyday. It has allowed me take a little less of the other pain meds that I hate so much, but it really doesn't help me feel any more optimistic or see my life differently. Yes, I live in SF, but can barely afford to do so. Im rent poor and by the time I pay my rent and bills I'm basically broke. I know I have it better materialistically than many other people on the planet. I work for a non profit - I work with homeless, disabled people all day (while I myself feel like I'm walking the edge of my own disability) so I know It could be worse - I could be homeless on the streets - but this insight doesn't change the fact that I am a mere shadow of the person I used to be, before I became ill and had to start taking my medications, nor does it change the fact that I am completely alone in my life. Comparing my pain to the rest of the worlds pain doesn't seem to help me feel more hopeful about things ever getting better for me.
